newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Suspicious package at U.N. turns out harmless.
newsitem.headline: Suspicious package at U.N. turns out harmless.

text.p: A suspicious package was screened near Secretary-General Kofi Annan's office on Wednesday but was found to be harmless, U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said.
He said the New York City bomb squad was called in again after four letter bombs were detected at U.N. headquarters on Monday.
But the package found on the 38th floor, where the secretary-general's offices are, "turned out not to be a bomb," Eckhard said.
Annan was not in his office when the alert was sounded, but was on his way down to a basement conference room, he said.
The four letter bombs found on Monday were addressed to the U.N. bureau of the Arabic-language newspaper Al-Hayat and bore Alexandria, Egypt, postmarks.
They were discovered several hours after a letter bomb exploded at the the newspaper's London headquarters, injuring two security guards.
